title: 第12章 宣传歌曲，做大做强
content_zh:
第12章 宣传歌曲，做大做强-《华娱2008：从分手快乐开始》

存书签

一曲终了，空气突然安静。

魏沐抬头看向对面三人，郑凯和杜姜陷入沉思，陈贺放下单反，轻轻扬起了大脑袋。

“哎呀，沙子有点多。”

虽然这样说，但陈赤赤眼角的泪水却出卖了他。

现在的大学生都这么感性吗？

这还是表演系的大学生呢。

说到底还是年轻啊。

在心里腹诽几句，魏沐跑过去拿起单反按下重播键。

今天这场表演一是气氛到这了，不得不来。

还有一个目的就是他想把唱歌的视频传到网上。

到时候与新歌同步发出，争取流量最大化，做大做强！

现在是2008年，网络视频野蛮生长的时代，也是网红扎堆出现的时代。

三年前，在广州美院的一个宿舍里，两个长相普通的男生以非常浮夸的表情“表演”潘伟博的成名曲《不得不爱》

说是表演，其实就是对口型，用后世的话说这就是一恶搞段子。

但就是这样毫无技术含量的视频，却风靡网络，打开了许多年轻人的新世界。

这对二人组，一个叫黄艺馨，一个叫韦炜，他们走红后签约了太和麦田，并且发了专辑，也参演了一些影视剧，可惜最后没什么水花，慢慢消失在网络海洋里。

当年陈刀仔.....啊呸.....后舍男孩能凭借搞笑段子，从无人问津的屌丝大学生一跃成为火爆全网的明星，我魏沐为什么不可以？

这年头，网红就像流星一样，刚出来的时候闪耀天际，然后便快速坠落。

不管现在还是未来都一样。

如果网红没有真材实料，最后只能泯然众人。

但魏沐不一样，他手上还有不少脍炙人口的歌曲，随便拿出来一个都不比《体面》差。

“老魏，你真牛逼，这首歌写的太好了！！”

陈贺激动的把他抱起来，让正在反复观看录像的魏沐吓一跳，手上的单反差点摔到地上。

“艹，你小心点，差点把你单反摔烂。”

“摔烂就摔烂吧，我再买一个，反正又不贵。”

陈贺这话没说错，2008年是全民单反时代，他年初买的这款索尼a200才三千多块钱。

三千多对他来说不算什么，但对普通人不算少。

魏沐在奉天工作的教职工父母，他们大半个月的工资也就这些钱。

扒拉开他的手，魏沐没好气白了他一眼。

这特娘是重点吗？

老子刚才发挥这么好，再让你录一遍，都没有这么好的效果。

The song ended and the air suddenly became quiet.

Wei Mu looked up at the three people opposite him. Zheng Kai and Du Jiang were deep in thought. Chen He put down his SLR and raised his big head slightly.

"Oops, there's a lot of sand."

Although he said this, the tears in the corners of Chen Chichi's eyes betrayed him.

Are all college students today so emotional?

This is a college student in the acting department.

After all, you are still young.

Cursing a few words in his mind, Wei Mu ran over, picked up the SLR, and pressed the replay button.

The atmosphere of today's performance has reached this point, so I had to come.

Another purpose is that he wants to post the singing video online.

When the time comes, it will be released simultaneously with the new song, striving to maximize traffic and make it bigger and stronger!

Now is 2008, an era when online videos are growing wildly, and it is also an era when Internet celebrities are appearing together.

Three years ago, in a dormitory of the Guangzhou Academy of Fine Arts, two ordinary-looking boys "performed" Pan Weibo's famous song "Have to Love" with very exaggerated expressions.

It's said to be a performance, but it's actually lip-syncing. In later generations' terms, it's a spoof.

But such a video with no technical content has become popular on the Internet and opened up a new world for many young people.

This duo, one named Huang Yixin and the other Wei Wei, signed a contract with Taihe Maitian after they became popular, released an album, and participated in some film and television dramas. Unfortunately, there was little splash in the end and they slowly disappeared into the Internet ocean.

Back then, Chen Daozai... ah... the boy in the back room could use his funny jokes to rise from an unnoticed college student to a popular star on the Internet. Why can't I, Wei Mu, do the same?

These days, Internet celebrities are like shooting stars, shining in the sky when they first appear, and then falling quickly.

It's the same now and in the future.

If Internet celebrities don’t have real materials, they will end up being ignored by everyone.

But Wei Mu is different. He still has many popular songs, and any one of them is no worse than "Decent".

"Lao Wei, you are so awesome, this song is so well written!!"

Chen He picked him up excitedly, which startled Wei Mu, who was watching the video repeatedly, and the SLR in his hand almost fell to the ground.

"Fuck, be careful, I almost broke your SLR."

"If it breaks, just break it. I'll buy another one. It's not expensive anyway."

Chen He was right. 2008 was the era of SLRs for all people. The Sony a200 he bought at the beginning of the year only cost more than 3,000 yuan.

More than three thousand is nothing to him, but it is not a small amount to ordinary people.

Wei Mu's parents, teachers and staff who work in Fengtian, only receive this amount of salary for most of the month.

Pulling his hand away, Wei Mu rolled his eyes at him angrily.

Is this special girl the point?

I played so well just now, and if I ask you to record it again, it won’t have such a good effect.
